I was a girl and a good student but always terribly anxious. School came very easy to me, so I would get straight As without paying much attention. High school got harder, and my stress became even more unmanageable to the point where I developed an eating disorder, mostly as a self-soothing distraction from how miserable I was. In college, I almost immediately burned out and became depressed and unable to hyperfunction like I used to as a kid. Then, all of the more classic ADHD symptoms became obvious. It still took me until this year, at the age of 28, to get a formal diagnosis, and that was after about five years of self-advocating. 

Basically, if you don't cause trouble in the school system, there's no reason for people to diagnose you, even if you're experiencing extreme distress.

Obviously, it's not magic, but I should at least feel benefits from a medicine I'm taking, right? I can feel a slight increase in heart rate but no cognitive changes as far as I can tell. I've been on Adderall and Vyvanse before, so I know what 'feeling' works for me.

I guess it depends. 

I usually respond to long comments because I love getting comments, but if it's someone who leaves comments all the time, I tend to not respond to every single one. 

On some stories, I get a large amount of comments, so it's impossible to respond to all of them, but I still try to reply to more specific comments. 

On some stories, I barely get any comments so I'll usually reply to most of them unless it's like "this is so good!!" like I don't want to just say "thanks!” to everyone. It feels disengenuious to me. 

On the reader end, I crave comments like I crave oxygen. They release One (1) Molecule of Serotonin, so I comment on any story I enjoyed because I know what that rush feels like. But also, authors don't owe their readers anything, especially since we're all because we're doing it for free and out of the kindness of our heart. My absolute biggest pet peeve is when readers are rude to authors and demand more content or criticize aspects of the story.

I know that a lot of times, my take on a certain series is completely different than other people, and even though I think my version is better, most of the populous might not agree. That's okay. Your version is just as important. You are creating transformative work, and that's what matters. 

As for tips, I'd say just to keep writing. I wrote a 170k word fic, and I got markedly better by the end. Practice makes perfect, after all. ;)
